<reason>CON won by shifting the question from urgency to effectiveness. PRO powerfully described housing pain and crisis risk, but CON showed rates do not build homes, cheaper prices do not equal affordability if incomes/jobs fall, and PRO's temporary-cost/permanent-benefit asymmetry was asserted not proved. PRO's admission it would tighten even at target over scarcity rents exposed a sectoral overreach CON exploited cleanly.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's scarcity-at-target Q1 forced PRO to say Yes and call the target a statistical illusion, which CON then used to show the priority means depressing jobs elsewhere for a shortage rates cannot fix.</best_rebuttal>
